data.headline: FedEx sees global demand holding amid Iran war, raises profit outlook
data.summary: STORY: FedEx said on Thursday that global demand is holding steady despite the war in Iran.CEO Raj Subramaniam said that demand for the first two weeks of March has been in line with FedEx's expectations.Executives said the Middle East accounts for a small part of the global delivery company.According to analysts, about 8% of FedEx's international export volume flows through hubs in the war-affected region.The company also reported strong fiscal earnings for the quarter ended February 28, helped by healthy delivery demand and cost controls during the pivotal holiday quarter.Subramaniam said the peak season was "the most profitable" in FedEx history.FedEx raised its full‑year profit forecast, sending shares up 9% in after‑hours trading.With the war in Iran, oil prices hit over $100 a barrel.But the shipping giant says the fuel surcharge it has in place is "doing its job." FedEx said its outlook assumes no additional geopolitical disruptions.But adds that the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran could weigh on fourth-quarter performance if soaring fuel costs prompt customers to pull back.
